architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated all GitHub Actions workflows to use the latest major versions of actions, with a focus on actions/setup-node@v6 to standardize on Node.js 22
architecture_decisions.rationale: The changes eliminate deprecation warnings by migrating from older action versions (v3-v5) to their latest stable releases. This ensures compatibility with GitHub's evolving platform, improves security with updated dependencies, and maintains consistent behavior across all workflows. The Node.js version was already at 22 in most workflows, so the focus was on updating the action versions rather than changing the Node version itself.
alternatives_considered: Updating only the setup-node action while leaving others unchanged
Switching to a different Node.js version manager or container-based approach
Creating a composite action to centralize Node.js setup across workflows

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Systematically updated all GitHub Action dependencies to their latest major versions across 12 workflow files
architecture_decisions.rationale: Bulk updates ensure consistency and reduce maintenance overhead. By updating all actions in a single change, we avoid version fragmentation and ensure all workflows benefit from the latest features, security patches, and performance improvements. This approach follows the principle of 'dependency hygiene' for CI/CD pipelines.
alternatives_considered: Gradual rollout updating one workflow at a time
Pinning to specific patch versions instead of major versions
Creating a shared action repository for common workflows

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Restructured release-drafter.yml to separate concerns between drafting releases and auto-labeling PRs
architecture_decisions.rationale: The workflow was split into two distinct jobs ('draft_release' and 'auto_label') with conditional execution based on event type. This improves clarity, reduces unnecessary job execution, and follows GitHub Actions best practices for event-driven workflows. The auto-labeler now runs only on pull_request events while release drafting runs on push/workflow_dispatch events.
alternatives_considered: Keeping a single job with complex conditional logic
Creating separate workflow files for different concerns
Using matrix strategies to handle different event types

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated security scanning workflows (CodeQL and Trivy) to use latest action versions
architecture_decisions.rationale: Security tools benefit most from staying current, as they receive frequent vulnerability database updates and scanning improvements. Updating github/codeql-action from v3 to v4 and maintaining trivy scanning ensures the project continues to receive the latest security analysis capabilities without breaking changes.
alternatives_considered: Keeping older versions for stability in security scanning
Switching to alternative security scanning tools
Disabling security scanning during the transition period

tickets.title: Update GitHub Actions to Latest Versions
tickets.description: Update all GitHub Actions workflow files to use the latest major versions of GitHub Actions, focusing on actions/setup-node@v6 and related dependencies

implementation_summary:
The implementation focused on modernizing the CI/CD pipeline by systematically updating all GitHub Actions workflows to their latest major versions. Contrary to the feature request's mention of updating to Node.js 24, the actual changes revealed that Node.js was already at version 22 in most workflows, so the primary focus became updating the GitHub Actions themselves rather than changing the Node version.

The changes follow a consistent pattern across 12 workflow files: updating actions/checkout from v4 to v6, actions/setup-node to v6, actions/cache to v5, and various other actions to their latest stable versions. This bulk update approach ensures consistency and reduces maintenance overhead. The most significant structural change was in release-drafter.yml, which was refactored into two separate jobs with conditional execution based on event type, improving clarity and efficiency.

These updates integrate seamlessly with the existing codebase because they maintain the same workflow logic and structure while only changing the action versions. The project's mature CI/CD infrastructure, with its extensive GitHub Actions setup, benefits from these updates through improved performance, security, and compatibility with GitHub's evolving platform. The changes demonstrate good dependency management practices by proactively updating CI/CD tools alongside application dependencies.
